stem.en: A rabbit hops across a yard to reach fresh grass. The cells of its leg muscles change shape again and again as it hops. Which feature of animal cells makes this change of shape easy?

text.en: They sit inside a hard, woody layer that bends them into new shapes.

feedback.en: No. A hard, woody layer would hold the cells stiff. Animal cells have no such layer.

text.en: They have no rigid cell wall, so nothing stiff holds them in one shape.

feedback.en: Yes. With no rigid wall around them, animal cells can change shape easily.

text.en: They have a thick cell wall that is soft enough to stretch whenever the animal moves its legs.

feedback.en: No. Animal cells have no cell wall at all. A cell wall is found in plant cells.

text.en: They make their own food, which gives them the energy to change shape.

feedback.en: No. Animal cells do not make their own food. Animals digest the food they eat.

hints.en: Think about what is around a plant cell but missing around an animal cell.
A stiff layer around a cell holds it in one shape.

explanation.en: Animal cells have no rigid cell wall. Without a wall, a cell can change shape easily, and this helps an animal's body to move. Plant cells are the opposite: their stiff walls hold each cell in shape, which keeps a plant firm and upright.
